policy-and-script-roles.text: The diagram links five roles. The registry identity names the configured application policy as its parameter. That policy mints action tokens named by a hash of the action and its parameters into request UTxOs. Folding runs the representative policy, which places the representative into the application spending script's output; that script releases it into an exact terminal request.
Roles may share a script hash; nothing requires or forbids it. The interface target is one parameter, the application policy ID, not yet proved sufficient.

what-insert-exposes-and-binds.text: The proposal exposes registry, operation and key, the approving policy and its evidence, the initial state, the destination and the output requirements. None is substitutable after certification. The action name hashes a domain-separated action and its parameters; Insert and Withdraw carry different tags.

validation-without-mutable-registry-obse.text: The sequence diagram shows three moments. At request creation the application policy validates facts, approval and construction without reading the registry root. At release the application spending script authorizes the transfer without reading it either. At consumption Singular's witnesses read the current state, recompute the certificate name and apply the operation.

which-script-actually-executes.text: Sending an output to a script address does not run that script; it runs when the output is consumed. The table assigns an executing witness to each boundary: minting an action asset, releasing an NFT, folding a request, withdrawing a pending Insert, and any nonzero net change of an action asset.
The mint field records net quantities, so a Delete and Insert on the same asset could cancel; the fold witnesses must still enforce both transitions.

decisions-still-required.text: Seven decisions remain, each with a constraint already fixed: configuration authenticity, Update and Delete token construction, encoding and lifecycle, withdrawal and refunds, identity across Delete and reinsert, batching, and implementation and shared libraries.

what-the-settled-interface-changes-here.text: The certification boundary on this page is the one the settled interface keeps: the application approves a request when the request is created, by minting an approval under its configured policy, and the fold checks only that the approval is there. The interface makes that the rule for every tree change, so an application is an approval minting policy plus its own output validators, and no script of the application's is ever present in a fold.

Two identities change shape. The representative policy becomes one of three token policies pinned beside the application policy at genesis: active, absent and terminal, each minting only inside a fold of its own cage. And the open update and delete request token construction is answered by the representative itself carrying the request, with no second token.

One decision in the table below is resolved: representative identity across delete and reinsert is the same identity. A deleted key is recreated as the same key, not versioned, and an application that wants a key never to return terminates it instead of deleting it.
